bhtStats.assetTitle: Asset used to measure subsequent performance
bhtStats.p1: The BHT Index measures market risk from 0 to 100: low (green) = cheap and calm, high (red) = expensive and dangerous.
bhtStats.p2: This table groups the days in the range by BHT level and shows what happened to the {asset} ({note}) over the following year and over 3 years (only days whose horizon has already elapsed): the worst (min), the typical (avg) and the best (max), plus the CAGR (average yearly return over 3 years).
bhtStats.p3spx: The reading is simple: when the BHT was low (20–35), the following year gained ~+37% on average; when it was high (65 or more), the following year barely gained or lost.
bhtStats.p3other: The reading is simple: compare the 1Y avg between low (green) and high (red) bands: if the green ones return much more, the BHT anticipates this asset well.
bhtStats.compass: Use it as a compass: <g>green = opportunity</g>, <r>red = caution</r>. Historical and hypothetical results; they do not guarantee future returns.
bhtStats.summaryBht: {from} → {to} · {n1} days with mature 1Y · {n3} with mature 3Y ({span}) · {asset} performance at 1 and 3 years by BHT band.
bhtStats.capeIntro: Same reading grouped by Shiller CAPE (price / 10-year earnings): low CAPE = cheap market, high CAPE = expensive market. Score = risk points contributed by that CAPE (0 cheap – 100 extreme).
bhtStats.summaryCape: {from} → {to} · {n1} days with CAPE and mature 1Y · {n3} with mature 3Y · {asset} performance at 1 and 3 years by CAPE.
